solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dog do Irish playwright bags

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it in a bag, so the playwright's name holds the other word inside it

blocks.note: George Bernard Shaw, the Dublin-born dramatist
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction about a dog's mess that an Irish dramatist pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog do' looks like one phrase about mess, but Dog is the definition, used as a verb, and do simply goes inside the playwright's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely, which is exactly what it means to shadow them.

clue.text: Poet in with Romeo

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A poet getting on well with Shakespeare's lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer is the ancient Greek poet credited with the Iliad and the Odyssey.

clue.text: Disavowals from Stormy Daniels

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the name's letters are tossed about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stormy Daniels, the woman in a famous lawsuit, issuing disavowals.
explanation.walkthrough: Stormy Daniels reads as a full name, but her first name is the instruction to rearrange the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A disavowal is a refusal to accept responsibility for something, which is a kind of denial.

clue.text: Insect losing tail is no more

indicators.note: losing its tail means the final letter of the insect's name is dropped

blocks.note: a wasp is a stinging insect

explanation.surface: A dead insect that has lost its tail end.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something was, in the past tense, implies it no longer exists, so it is no more.

clue.text: Cruel sort, it is time to arrest duke

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold someone captive, so the earlier letters hold the duke within them

blocks.note: it in the sense of sex appeal, abbreviated SA
taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A cruel person announcing it is time to arrest a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes between SA and IST. 'It' for sex appeal (SA) is an old convention from the phrase 'she's got it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist is someone who takes pleasure in inflicting pain, a cruel type of person.

clue.text: Bloomer in tabloid — female let down

blocks.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
F is the abbreviation for female
to let something down is to lower it

explanation.surface: A tabloid reporting a blunder after a woman was disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomer suggests a blunder, the British sense of an embarrassing mistake, but here it is literally something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer, read literally, is a plant that flowers, and the sunflower is a large flowering plant.

clue.text: Silly involving two Zulus in do-it-yourself

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the do-it-yourself letters surround the two Zulus

blocks.note: DIY is the common abbreviation for do-it-yourself
Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet, so two of them make ZZ

explanation.surface: Something foolish happening with two Zulu men doing their own home improvements.
explanation.definitionFit: Dizzy is used informally of a scatterbrained, giddy person, much the same as silly.

clue.text: Dried fruit for Ottoman lady

blocks.note: first meaning: a pale seedless raisin
second meaning: the wife, mother or daughter of a sultan

explanation.surface: Offering dried fruit to a woman of the Turkish court.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a light raisin and the wife or female relative of an Ottoman sultan.

clue.text: Criminal unnamed holds South Polar explorer

indicators.note: criminal means crooked or wrong, so the following word's letters are put in a different order
to hold something is to have it inside, so the jumbled word contains the compass point

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: An anonymous criminal has the South Pole explorer captive.
explanation.walkthrough: South looks like it belongs with Polar, but it is only the letter S going into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Amundsen was the Norwegian explorer who led the first expedition to reach the South Pole, in 1911.

clue.text: Snake-haired female leaves cheese for French writer

indicators.note: when something leaves it departs, so that word is taken away from the cheese's name

blocks.note: Gorgonzola is an Italian blue cheese
a Gorgon, like Medusa, had living snakes for hair

explanation.surface: A Medusa-like woman walking out on cheese in favour of a French author.
explanation.definitionFit: Emile Zola was a French novelist, author of Germinal and the open letter J'accuse.

clue.text: Killer inside Windsor Castle

indicators.note: inside says the letters sit within the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A murderer lurking within Windsor Castle, the royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: Killer reads as a murderer; it is the killer whale.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca is commonly called the killer whale, a large predator of the dolphin family.

clue.text: Charlie to feed a stray lately — feline one?

indicators.note: feeding something means putting it inside, so the letter goes into the middle of the rest
to stray is to wander off course, so these letters wander out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone has been feeding a stray cat recently, and it turns out to be feline.
explanation.walkthrough: Stray looks like the cat being fed, but it is the signal to rearrange. The question mark admits the definition is by example: not every feline is one.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley cat is a stray or homeless urban cat, so it is one kind of feline.

clue.text: Great ruler in a country invaded by former queen

indicators.note: a country that is invaded has someone come inside it, so the next word goes within it

blocks.note: taken as written
a land is a country
an ex is a former partner, so ex means former
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A great ruler in a land overrun by a deposed queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former queen' reads as one deposed monarch, but the two words work separately, one going inside the country and the other tacked on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great was the Macedonian king who ruled an empire stretching from Greece to India.

clue.text: Scots girl sails terribly close to shore

indicators.note: terribly means badly done, so the word's letters are sent into a disordered state
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of shore

explanation.surface: A Scottish girl sails very badly, too near the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to shore' reads as a sailing position, but it means the last letter of shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie is the Scots and northern English word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: American paper under discussion

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
tissue is thin soft paper

explanation.surface: An American newspaper being talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: Paper suggests a newspaper, but it is tissue paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is the point currently being debated or in dispute, the subject under discussion.

clue.text: Reproductive organ primarily adapted to marsupial

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of each of the next words is used

blocks.note: the womb is the female reproductive organ
the first letters of adapted and to

explanation.surface: A reproductive organ that has evolved mainly to suit a pouched mammal.
explanation.walkthrough: A marsupial's pouch makes the surface plausible, but the organ simply supplies the first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The wombat is a burrowing Australian animal that carries its young in a pouch, a marsupial.

clue.text: Chinese dynasty ruled and was sociable

blocks.note: the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644
to rule is to lead, so ruled is led

explanation.surface: A Chinese dynasty that held power and got on well with people.
explanation.definitionFit: To mingle is to circulate and mix with others at a gathering, so having mingled is having been sociable.

clue.text: Monster child devouring Greek character

indicators.note: devouring means eating up, so the child takes the Greek character inside it

blocks.note: a minor is a child in law
tau is the Greek letter T

explanation.surface: A monstrous child eating a Greek letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Minotaur ate Athenian youths, so 'devouring' neatly echoes the myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minotaur was the bull-headed creature of Greek myth kept in the Cretan labyrinth, a monster.

clue.text: One spreading legs — it may cause tears

indicators.note: spreading legs means pushing them apart, so the one goes between the two of them

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side, so each leg is ON, and legs gives two of them
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone doing the splits, which may well bring tears to the eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the leg side of the field is also called the on side, which is why leg gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping an onion releases a compound that irritates the eyes and makes them water.

clue.text: Grandmother beginning to annoy idiot

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is taken here

blocks.note: nan is an informal word for a grandmother
the first letter of annoy

explanation.surface: An elderly relative starting to irritate a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Grandmother looks like the definition, since the answer is also a word for one, but here it is the wordplay and idiot is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nana is informal British slang for a silly or foolish person, as in 'don't be a nana'.

clue.text: Hotel occupies lovely position

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to be inside it, so the hotel letter sits within the next word

blocks.note: nice means pleasant or lovely
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel standing in a beautiful spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a role or place suited to someone, as in finding one's niche in a career.

clue.text: Stone dropped into excellent wine

indicators.note: something dropped into a thing ends up inside it, so the stone goes within the word for excellent

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as the letter I
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A pebble falls into a glass of fine wine.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight (14 pounds), abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from the Piedmont region of Italy.

clue.text: Lifeless hair — intractable problem

blocks.note: lifeless means dead
a lock is a strand of hair

explanation.surface: Limp, lank hair is a problem that won't go away.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a standstill where neither side will give way, a problem with no way through.

clue.text: Bird among skuas heading north

indicators.note: among says the letters are found within the word that follows
in a down entry, heading north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A bird flying north with a flock of skuas.
explanation.definitionFit: The auk is a black and white diving seabird of northern waters, such as the razorbill.

clue.text: Male voice on the radio for £10

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: the tenor is the highest common adult male singing voice

explanation.surface: A male singer performs on the radio for a ten-pound fee.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenner is the informal British word for ten pounds or a ten-pound note.

clue.text: Dye and ink misused in class

indicators.note: misused means used wrongly, so the letters are put to work in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dye and ink are wasted during a school lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: Class suggests a school lesson, but it is the old sense of kind or type.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidney is an old word for sort or temperament, as in 'a man of that kidney', so it means class.
